interim_updates.note_text: LMF Group revenue grew 25.3% YoY to Rs 5.85bn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), with growth led by the Liquid Milk and Others segment (UHT products, 'Daily', 'Ambewela Farm Fresh Milk', yogurt and fruit juice), which grew revenue 30.7% (Rs 3.30bn to Rs 4.31bn) and remains the largest segment at 73.7% of total revenue. The Powdered Milk segment grew revenue 25.7% (Rs 1.19bn to Rs 1.49bn) and the Agriculture segment (livestock/cattle rearing) grew a slower 2.6% (Rs 1.61bn to Rs 1.65bn). Group gross profit grew 21.9% to Rs 1.17bn and operating profit (profit from operations) grew 16.9% to Rs 678mn -- both below the pace of revenue growth, reflecting a Rs 969mn (26.1%) rise in cost of sales that slightly outpaced the 25.3% revenue increase. By segment, profit from operations at Liquid Milk and Others surged 50.8% (Rs 378mn to Rs 570mn), the single largest contributor to the Group's operating profit growth, while the Agriculture segment's operating profit fell 59.7% (Rs 136mn to Rs 55mn) -- and, further down the P&L, the Agriculture segment's net finance expense worsened from Rs 138mn to Rs 187mn, pushing the segment from a Rs 14.6mn net loss for the period a year ago to a Rs 151.2mn net loss this quarter (a swing of roughly Rs 136.6mn), which was more than offset at the Group level by the Rs 168.5mn increase in Liquid Milk and Others segment profit. Group PBT grew a more modest 13.5% to Rs 560mn (below operating profit growth) because Group net finance expense worsened from Rs 87mn to Rs 118mn, and Group PAT grew 12.4% to Rs 424mn; basic EPS rose 12.8% to Rs 1.06. At the standalone Company level, revenue grew 22.4% and PBT grew a slower 8.1% (Rs 99mn to Rs 107mn), but Company PAT grew a faster 34.3% (Rs 78mn to Rs 105mn) because the Company's own income tax expense fell sharply, from Rs 21.2mn to Rs 2.5mn (-88.2% YoY) -- a standalone-level tax swing not mirrored at the Group level, where consolidated tax expense actually rose 17.1% to Rs 136mn.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for LMF -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. YoY comparison uses the filing's own prior-year comparative column (three months ended 30 June 2025). The filing's own balance-sheet comparative is versus 31 March 2026 (FYE), not 30 June 2025, consistent with standard interim SOFP presentation -- this is NOT used for any QoQ purpose, only as the filing's own point-in-time comparative.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline Group growth (revenue +25%, PAT +12%) is real but the two halves of the business are diverging sharply: the Liquid Milk and Others segment (UHT/Daily/Ambewela) is the clear growth engine, with operating profit up 51% YoY, while the Agriculture (livestock) segment's net loss for the period nearly tripled in size YoY (from Rs 14.6mn to Rs 151.2mn) on rising finance costs -- without the Liquid Milk segment's strength, Group profit growth would have been far weaker or negative.
operational_highlights: Group revenue +25.3% YoY to Rs 5.85bn; Group PAT +12.4% YoY to Rs 423.9mn; basic EPS +12.8% to Rs 1.06
Liquid Milk and Others segment (UHT, Daily, Ambewela Farm Fresh Milk, yogurt, juice) revenue +30.7% YoY to Rs 4.31bn, 73.7% of Group revenue; segment operating profit +50.8% to Rs 570mn
Powdered Milk segment revenue +25.7% YoY to Rs 1.49bn
Agriculture (livestock) segment swung to a larger net loss for the period: Rs 151.2mn vs Rs 14.6mn a year earlier, as segment net finance expense worsened from Rs 138mn to Rs 187mn
Group cost of sales rose 26.1% YoY (Rs 3.71bn to Rs 4.68bn), slightly outpacing revenue growth and compressing gross margin from 20.6% to 20.0%
Company (standalone) PAT +34.3% YoY to Rs 104.9mn, faster than Group, as standalone income tax expense fell 88.2% YoY (Rs 21.2mn to Rs 2.5mn) even as standalone PBT grew only 8.1%
key_drivers: Liquid Milk and Others segment operating profit +50.8% YoY (Rs 378mn to Rs 570mn) is the single largest driver of Group operating profit growth

Agriculture (livestock) segment net loss for the period nearly tripled YoY (Rs 14.6mn to Rs 151.2mn), driven by segment net finance expense worsening from Rs 138mn to Rs 187mn -- a meaningful drag that was more than offset by the Liquid Milk segment
Group net finance expense worsened 35.7% YoY (Rs 86.9mn to Rs 118.0mn), causing PBT growth (13.5%) to lag operating profit growth (16.9%)

Standalone Company income tax expense fell 88.2% YoY (Rs 21.2mn to Rs 2.5mn), a divergence from the Group's 17.1% tax expense increase, driving standalone PAT growth (34.3%) well above standalone PBT growth (8.1%)
